title: repo_orientation — a box-written map of one repository at main (more-local-inference 10)
description: What a local model found about how one repository is laid out and works: its modules, the conventions a change has to follow, where the tests live and the commands that run them, and the traps a newcomer hits. `gate` requires every cited path to exist in the checkout and holds the rendered map to 6,000 characters. `post` writes it as the body of the repository's one pinned `fabro-orientation` issue, which `backlog`'s and `ralph`'s `prep` copy to /tmp/fabro/orientation.md for `decompose` and `plan`. _io is stamped by the server and is not part of this schema.

summary.description: Two or three sentences: what this repository is, and how a change usually gets made in it. Published verbatim.

modules.description: The parts of the repository a change lands in, biggest first. A path that does not exist is dropped before anyone sees the map.

path.description: Repository-relative directory or file, exactly as in the checkout.

what.description: One line: what lives there and what it is responsible for.

conventions.description: The rules a change in this repository follows that a newcomer would get wrong: naming, layering, error handling, where a new file goes, what must be updated with it.

tests.description: Where the tests live and what each kind covers.

commands.description: The commands this repository runs, exactly as its own configuration runs them (`Makefile`, `package.json`, `pyproject.toml`, `.fabro/ci.sh`), and what each is for.

gotchas.description: Traps that cost a newcomer a run: a generated file, a second copy of the same logic, a test that needs a service, a directory that looks authoritative and is not.
